title: Extreme Unit-Level Panel IV Estimates under Weak First Stages and Heavy-Tailed Effects

proof_attempt_summary: D0 discharged the exact Gaussian experiment's phase diagram, boundary inference, and cutoff in the discovery note. The D0.5 math panel passed with no findings, but the general referee graded the delivered package incremental because transfer to an actual panel-IV estimator remains open. A future field-tier attempt needs a substantive general-panel approximation or comparable external-validity result; the decision panel's related-work omission remains unrepaired.
tldr: Unit-wise panel-IV extremes can be generated either by genuinely large causal effects or by estimated first stages crossing zero. In the exact Gaussian triangular experiment, the project derives their joint signed marked Poisson limit, with positive exceedance measure \(x^{-\kappa}+\lambda/x\), and shows that a nontrivial constant-tail-coefficient three-phase frontier exists only for \(\kappa>1\). The same law yields boundary-aware extreme-quantile inference and a feasible pole-intensity estimator under the scoped restrictions \(\theta_i\perp\pi_i\) and known \(\kappa\). A symmetric cutoff \(|D_i|\ge T^{-1/2}/\log N\) removes pole extremes while preserving the unconditional structural extreme process under arbitrary coefficient-strength dependence. Transfer to actual panel estimators is posed separately as a uniform local-Gaussian-approximation problem.
gap: Existing noisy-extreme theory determines when estimation noise is negligible, and classical ratio theory characterizes a single Gaussian ratio. Neither literature characterizes the cross-sectional boundary at which structural extreme effects and weak-first-stage denominator poles coexist.
fill: The project derives the signed superposition and polynomial \(N\)-versus-\(T\) frontier, constructs boundary critical values and a feasible intensity estimate, proves a target-preserving cutoff, and isolates the local-limit theorem required before any general-panel claim is valid.
